info.title: OpenLaw API
info.description: REST API for OpenLaw. Also the third-party integration surface (TECH-003).

get.summary: Instance metadata
The signed-in user, with their live role and session

patch.summary: Update the signed-in user's preferences (theme #44, timezone SET-006)

get.summary: Whether first-run setup (initial Administrator) is still required

post.summary: First-run setup: create the initial Administrator

get.summary: What the login screen may offer (TECH-008): the auth mode, the magic-link toggle, whether outbound email works, and the SSO provider to start, if one is registered

post.summary: Invite a user (Administrator, Legal Team Member, or Contributor); re-sends the set-password email if they have not activated
Re-send a pending invite's set-password email (SET-005)

delete.summary: Revoke a pending invite (SET-005): the row is removed and the emailed set-password link stops working

post.summary: Register a bring-your-own OIDC identity provider (TECH-008); endpoint discovery runs from the issuer, and the response carries the callback URL to paste into the IdP console

get.summary: The registered OIDC identity providers (TECH-008), with their client IDs but never their secrets

patch.summary: Update the registered provider (TECH-008): omitted fields keep their stored values, endpoint discovery re-runs from the issuer, and a failed update leaves the provider untouched

get.summary: The organization's auth mode (TECH-008)

patch.summary: Switch the auth mode (TECH-008): `oidc` closes password sign-in for everyone but Administrators (break-glass); switching never invalidates existing sessions

get.summary: The magic-link domain allowlist (DD-010); empty admits nobody

put.summary: Replace the magic-link domain allowlist (DD-010); the list is normalised to lower case and enforced on the next request — an empty list closes the portal to everyone

patch.summary: Open or close magic-link sign-in (DD-010's portal floor); takes effect on the next request, independent of the domain allowlist

post.summary: Request a portal magic link (DD-010); the response is identical whether or not the address is eligible

get.summary: First-run onboarding state (SET-004), plus whether email is configured

post.summary: Mark first-run onboarding finished (SET-004); idempotent, and never reversed — the wizard is first-run only

get.summary: The organization's identity (SET-001 General pane)

patch.summary: Update the organization's identity; applies immediately (SET-003) and appends one audit entry per changed field

get.summary: Every user with role, status, and last-active (SET-005); pending invites appear as rows with status `invited`

patch.summary: Change a user's role in place (SET-005); effective on the target's next request — the guard chain reads the role live

post.summary: Archive a user (SET-005): sign-in is blocked and every live session is revoked in the same operation
Restore an archived user (SET-003's recovery story): sign-in works again; the sessions archive revoked stay revoked
Revoke every live session of a user (SET-005's lost-laptop case); the account itself is untouched

get.summary: Where outbound email is configured (#37): environment, app, or not at all — and the effective from-address. Never the relay URL

put.summary: Save the app SMTP relay (#37): smtp:// or smtps:// URL with credentials inline, plus a from-address; both null clears. Takes effect on the next send. Refused while the environment pins SMTP — env always wins over app configuration

post.summary: Send a test email through the currently resolved mailer to the signed-in Administrator's own address (#37); fails loudly with a plain-language reason

get.summary: The contract type taxonomy in display order (CTR-002); archived rows only with includeArchived=true

post.summary: Add a contract type: the slug is derived here, once, and is immutable after creation; the row appends to the display order

get.summary: One contract type — the read behind the type editor

patch.summary: Rename a contract type's display name (DES-017 in-place rename) or edit its description; the slug never changes, and even `other` may rename

delete.summary: Hard-delete a contract type; `other` refuses (CTR-002), and once contracts exist (M8) an in-use type will refuse too

put.summary: Apply a full permutation of the live rows (SET-003 immediate apply); display orders renumber from 1, archived rows keep theirs

post.summary: Archive a contract type (SET-003 guarded): it leaves pickers and the default list; nothing is deleted; `other` refuses
Restore an archived contract type (SET-003's recovery story) to the end of the display order

get.summary: One contract type's attached fields in per-type order — the type editor's Attached fields card

post.summary: Attach a catalog field to a contract type: contract-scoped and global fields only (CTR-016), appended to the per-type order, optional from the start unless isRequired says otherwise

patch.summary: Set an attachment's required flag: per attachment, so a field can be required for one type and optional elsewhere; hard enforcement arrives with the record milestone (M8)

delete.summary: Detach a field from a contract type: the join row goes, the catalog definition and stored values stay (MTR-014)

put.summary: Apply a full permutation of one type's attached fields (SET-003 immediate apply); per-type orders renumber from 1

get.summary: One matter type — the read behind the type editor

patch.summary: Rename a matter type's display name (DES-017 in-place rename) or edit its description; the slug never changes, and even `other` may rename

delete.summary: Hard-delete a matter type; `other` refuses (MTR-001), and once matters exist (M22) an in-use type will refuse too

put.summary: Apply a full permutation of the live rows (SET-003 immediate apply); display orders renumber from 1, archived rows keep theirs

Restore an archived matter type (SET-003's recovery story) to the end of the display order

get.summary: One matter type's attached fields in per-type order — the type editor's Attached fields card

post.summary: Attach a catalog field to a matter type: global fields only until M22 opens the matter scope (MTR-011), appended to the per-type order, optional from the start unless isRequired says otherwise

patch.summary: Set an attachment's required flag: per attachment, so a field can be required for one type and optional elsewhere; hard enforcement arrives with the record milestone (M22)

delete.summary: Detach a field from a matter type: the join row goes, the catalog definition and stored values stay (MTR-014)

put.summary: Apply a full permutation of one type's attached fields (SET-003 immediate apply); per-type orders renumber from 1

get.summary: The contract-status taxonomy in display order (CTR-001), each row carrying its fixed stage; archived rows only with includeArchived=true

post.summary: Add a contract status: the stage is picked here, once, and is immutable after creation, like the derived slug; the row appends to the display order

patch.summary: Rename a contract status's display name (DES-017 in-place rename); the slug and the stage never change — a body carrying `stage` is refused, and even protected rows may rename

delete.summary: Hard-delete a contract status; the protected `draft`, `active`, and `expired` rows refuse (CTR-001), as does the last unarchived status of a stage

put.summary: Apply a full permutation of the live rows (SET-003 immediate apply); display orders renumber from 1, archived rows keep theirs

post.summary: Archive a contract status (SET-003): it leaves pickers and the default list; nothing is deleted. The last unarchived status of a stage refuses (CTR-001 floor), as do the protected `draft`, `active`, and `expired` rows — no reassignment, ever
Restore an archived contract status (SET-003's recovery story) to the end of the display order; its stage rides along unchanged

get.summary: The contract list, newest reference first: number, title, type, and status; archived contracts only with includeArchived=true

post.summary: Create a contract from a title and a live type; the status starts on the protected draft seed (CTR-001) and the number comes from the CTR-003 sequence. Everything else is set inline on the record afterward

get.summary: The live contract types and statuses in display order, and the live people the Owner and team pickers offer — the create dialog's and the record's Member+ picker source (the settings surfaces stay Administrator-only per SET-002)
One contract by its CTR-003 number, with its Owner and its working group — the record page's read; archived contracts answer too, so restore stays reachable

patch.summary: Commit one field of a contract in place (DES-017 per-field commits): title, description, the Owner, priority, risk, or the status — any live status may follow any other (CTR-001). Never on an archived contract

post.summary: Put a person on the contract team under a role (CTR-004). The key is contract + person + role, so the same person may hold two roles; the `creator` role is the server's to write

delete.summary: Take one role off the contract team (CTR-004). The role is part of the address, so dropping a watcher leaves that same person's member row standing; `creator` is provenance and stays

post.summary: Archive a contract (soft delete, for mistakes and imports — not the same as ending it): it leaves the default list and freezes; nothing is deleted, and restore is the way back
Restore an archived contract (archive's recovery story): it rejoins the list and becomes editable again

get.summary: The entity type taxonomy in display order (ENT-001); archived rows only with includeArchived=true

post.summary: Add an entity type: the slug is derived here, once, and is immutable after creation; the row appends to the display order

get.summary: One entity type — the read behind the type editor

patch.summary: Rename an entity type's display name (DES-017 in-place rename) or edit its description; the slug never changes, and even `other` may rename

delete.summary: Hard-delete an entity type; `other` refuses (ENT-001), and so does a type still used by entities

put.summary: Apply a full permutation of the live rows (SET-003 immediate apply); display orders renumber from 1, archived rows keep theirs

post.summary: Archive an entity type (SET-003 guarded): a type still used by entities requires a reassignment target, which takes them; nothing is deleted; `other` refuses
Restore an archived entity type (SET-003's recovery story) to the end of the display order

get.summary: The registry, ordered by legal name (ENT-001) — the seam the M8 signing-entity picker consumes; archived rows only with includeArchived=true

post.summary: Register an entity with its ENT-001 identity card: legal name and type required, the rest optional; status defaults to active

get.summary: The live entity types in display order — the register form's Member+ picker source (the /entity-types settings surface stays Administrator-only per SET-002)
One entity's full ENT-001 identity card — the record page's read; archived entities answer too, so restore stays reachable

patch.summary: Correct any identity-card field in place (DES-017 per-field commits): the status only within the fixed ENT-001 enum, the type only to a live one, never on an archived entity

post.summary: Archive an entity (soft delete, ENT-001): it leaves the list and the M8 picker; nothing is deleted, and #99's restore is the recovery story
Restore an archived entity (archive's recovery story, ENT-001): it rejoins the list and the M8 picker

get.summary: The shared field catalog (CTR-016) scoped to contract and global fields, in creation order; archived rows only with includeArchived=true

post.summary: Define a field: the slug derives from the name and the field type is picked here, once — both are immutable after creation. Select types take their options list; an AI prompt rides on contract-scoped fields only (CTR-008)

patch.summary: Rename, describe, retag, or edit a field's options and AI prompt; the slug and the field type never change, and the scope moves through its own route — a body carrying any of them is refused, not silently stripped

put.summary: Move a field's scope (CTR-016): promotion to global is always safe (values stay keyed by slug); any move into a module is refused while another module attaches the field

post.summary: Archive a field (SET-003): it leaves the catalog and every form; the definition and all stored values are retained (MTR-014) — there is no hard delete
Restore an archived field (SET-003's recovery story): it rejoins the catalog under its original slug
